chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who presents (or supplicates for) forty from the believers, then supplicates (for himself), it will be answered for him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ: Forty, a significant number in Islamic tradition often denoting a complete group or congregation.
key_terms.اسْتُجِيبَ: It was answered, passive form of istijabah (acceptance of du'a).
key_terms.قَدَّمَ: To present, offer, or precede; in this context, it refers to presenting the believers or their merits before God.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of having forty believers in one's supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the communal nature of divine acceptance, where the presence or intercession of forty believers acts as a spiritual catalyst for the supplicant's request. This concept reflects the broader theological principle that the collective merit (fadl) of the righteous can elevate individual devotion, a theme often discussed in the context of congregational prayers and communal supplications (du'a).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who (supplicates for) forty from the Momineen (priorly), then supplicates (for himself), it will be Answered for him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever prays for forty believing persons and then for himself, his prayer will be accepted.’”
